_schema: Championship-season calendar for the service-time rewrite.
One row per season, from the earliest season a stored player debuted
(1986) through 2026. This file is reference data. The service-time
calculator does not read it.
Each row is taken from the MLB Stats API schedule (sportId 1,
gameType R). The request URL is stored on the row as source.
A game's date is its officialDate. Listings that were postponed,
cancelled, or a later duplicate of a resumed game are ignored.
Postseason games are not in this feed.
championship_start is the first game played anywhere, including a
series in Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney, Mexico, or San Juan.
first_domestic_game is the first game in the United States or Canada.
Those two dates differ only when games_outside_us_and_canada is set.
championship_end is the last regularly scheduled game. A tiebreaker
(a game the feed marks tiebreaker Y) counts only when it was played
after every other regular-season game; those games are listed in
tiebreakers_excluded and are not part of championship_end. A
tiebreaker flag on an ordinary mid-season date is not a game 163
and does not move the end. Rainout makeups stay in, because a
postponed game that was played later was still a scheduled game.
championship_days is the inclusive number of days from
championship_start through championship_end. A documented special
year may store a different count when its note explains why; every
other year matches the dates.
club_openers maps an MLB club id to that club's own first played
game. It is here so a staggered domestic opener can be compared
with the league-wide start. club_names gives the club's name as of
the latest season in this file; ids are stable across renames.
special is true when the season's length or its start was out of
the ordinary (a strike, a lockout, the 2020 cut to 60 games, the
September 2001 stoppage, or an opener outside the United States
and Canada that stretches the calendar). A special row carries a
note. A row that is not special runs 181 to 187 days. 2022 is
special even though its length is inside that range, because the
lockout moved the start.
games_played counts played games inside the championship season,
not the excluded tiebreakers.

seasons.notes: The 1990 owner lockout delayed the start. The first game was 1990-04-09 and the last was 1990-10-03 (178 championship-season days). The feed records 2105 played games, a full slate pushed into a shorter calendar.

The players' strike began on August 12. The last games were 1994-08-11. The rest of the schedule, the postseason, and the World Series were not played. The feed records 1600 played games across 131 days, from 1994-04-03.

After the strike settlement, clubs played a 144-game season. The first game was 1995-04-25 and the last regularly scheduled game was 1995-10-01 (160 championship-season days; 2016 played games in the feed). The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (1995-10-02 (California Angels at Seattle Mariners)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.
The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (1998-09-28 (San Francisco Giants at Chicago Cubs)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.

The season opened on April 4 with the Rockies at the Padres in Monterrey, Mexico. The first game in the United States or Canada was April 5. The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (1999-10-04 (Single-Game Playoff for NL Wildcard Berth)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.

seasons.notes: The Cubs and the Mets opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 29 and 30. The first game in the United States or Canada was April 3. The last regularly scheduled game was 2000-10-01 (187 days).

The season opened on April 1 with the Rangers at the Blue Jays in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The first game in the United States or Canada was April 2. No games were played from September 11 through September 16. Play resumed September 17, and makeup games pushed the last regularly scheduled date to 2001-10-07 (190 championship-season days).

The Yankees and the Devil Rays opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 30 and 31. The first game in the United States or Canada was April 4. The last regularly scheduled game was 2004-10-03 (188 days from the Tokyo opener).
The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (2007-10-01 (San Diego Padres at Colorado Rockies)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.

The Red Sox and the Athletics opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 25 and 26. The first game in the United States or Canada was March 30. The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (2008-09-30 (AL Central tiebreaker)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.
The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (2009-10-06 (AL Central Tiebreaker)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.

The Mariners and the Athletics opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 28 and 29. The first game in the United States or Canada was April 4. The last regularly scheduled game was 2012-10-03 (190 days from the Tokyo opener).
The schedule feed marks a tiebreaker after the last regularly scheduled date (2013-09-30 (AL Tiebreaker Game)). That game is not part of the championship-season end.

The Dodgers and the Diamondbacks opened at the Sydney Cricket Ground on March 22 and 23. The first game in the United States or Canada was March 30. The last regularly scheduled game was 2014-09-28 (191 days from the Sydney opener).
The first game anywhere was 2016-04-03. The Minnesota Twins' own first game was 2016-04-04, a day later, along with several other clubs. The league-wide start is the earlier date.

The schedule feed marks tiebreakers after the last regularly scheduled date (2018-10-01 (NL West tiebreaker); 2018-10-01 (NL Central tiebreaker)). Those games are not part of the championship-season end.

The Mariners and the Athletics opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 20 and 21. The first game in the United States or Canada was March 28. The last regularly scheduled game was 2019-09-29 (194 days from the Tokyo opener).

COVID-19 cut the season to 60 games a club. The first game was July 23 and the last was September 27 (67 championship-season days). The feed records 898 played games. Service for 2020 was prorated, so a player rostered for the whole season was credited a full year rather than the raw day count.

One April 11 game (Marlins at Mets) carries the schedule feed's tiebreaker flag, but it was a regularly scheduled game on a day the rest of the league also played. It stays inside the championship season and does not move the end date. The last regularly scheduled game was 2021-10-03.

The owner lockout delayed the start. The first game was 2022-04-07 and the last was 2022-10-05 (182 championship-season days). Clubs still played a full schedule (2430 played games). The Tigers opened on 2022-04-08 and the White Sox opened on 2022-04-08, a day after the first game.

The Dodgers and the Padres opened at Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul on March 20 and 21. The first game in the United States or Canada was March 28. The last regularly scheduled game was 2024-09-30, including the September 30 makeup games (195 days from the Seoul opener).

The Dodgers and the Cubs opened at the Tokyo Dome on March 18 and 19. Shohei Ohtani's club, the Dodgers, played in that series, so the league-wide start is the Tokyo date. The first game in the United States or Canada was March 27. The last regularly scheduled game was 2025-09-28 (195 days from the Tokyo opener).

The first game was the Yankees at the Giants at Oracle Park in San Francisco on 2026-03-25. That is a domestic game, so the league-wide start and the first domestic game are the same day. The Colorado Rockies, Jordan Beck's club, opened on 2026-03-27.
